deities: Lord Mahadev (dedicatory - this is primarily a royal memorial, not a functioning worship temple)

history.summary: MEMORIAL, NOT A FUNCTIONING HINDU TEMPLE: Kirti Mandir ('Temple of Fame') is the cenotaph of the Gaekwad royal family, built in 1936 by Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad III as part of his Diamond Jubilee celebrations to perpetuate the memory of his ancestors (the edifice is dedicated to Lord Mahadev). It has an E-shaped Indo-Saracenic plan with a ~35-metre central shikhara topped by a bronze finial depicting the sun, moon and earth with an undivided map of India. The marble-finished interiors hold murals by Nandalal Bose (Mahabharata battle, Gangavataran, Mirabai's life, Natir Pooja) plus paintings by Raja Ravi Varma and busts of Gaekwad rulers. It now serves as a cultural hub, hosting the famous annual Diwali Rangoli exhibition.

name: Kirti Mandir, Vadodara
town_description: Vadodara (formerly Baroda) is a major city in Gujarat on the Vishwamitri river, famed as the cultural capital of the state. It was the seat of the Gaekwad rulers, whose patronage left palaces, museums and temples across the city. Kirti Mandir stands near the Vishwamitri Bridge on Kothi Road, Sayajigunj, in the city centre.

travel.road: Kothi Road, Sayajigunj, near the Vishwamitri Bridge; in the heart of the city, combinable with nearby attractions like Laxmi Vilas Palace

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Diwali for the annual Rangoli exhibition
